cells.tense: What you celebrate with other people lands as a gathering, not a scattering.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: While clearing what is over, pull the loose thoughts about it into a single line you can hold. Let it sit overnight before you decide anything with it.
cells.core:
What you celebrate with people multiplies it. A thing is funnier, more real, easier to carry when someone else is nearby, and that is working where it is working. There is an ending close by, and the thoughts about it are spread across weeks and rooms right now.

The ease comes from drawing those loose threads into one line — not settling them for good, just enough of a line that you can say what this was. What you know and what you feel can sit in the same sentence. Once the line holds, joy has somewhere to stand rather than running loose, and the people you celebrate with get the gathered version of you.
cells.sheetLine: You gather the loose thoughts into one line, and joy stands on it.
cells.verb: carrying joy that comes alive only when it is shared
cells.place: at the point where something is over and the clearing has not been done

cells.tense: The ending is being survived before it has happened, and nothing lets it land.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Choose the closing that keeps getting postponed and do one small real piece of it today — a call, a box, a page. Then the same amount tomorrow.
cells.core:
Where you celebrate with people, the joy is being spent before it is earned. The ending is managed ahead of time — what you will say, how they will take it, what comes after — so nothing you are inside of gets to be what it is. You are at the doorway already planning the far room, and the doorway is not finishing.

The joy was not the plan for afterward. It is the sharing happening now, with the people who are here, while something is yet up. Letting it end will not cost you them. Doing today's part of the closing, small, without dressing it up, is the way the doorway completes.
cells.sheetLine: You are hedging the ending in advance, and it will not close.
cells.verb: carrying joy that comes alive only when it is shared
cells.place: at the point where something is over and the clearing has not been done

cells.tense: The ending is already behind you and the doorway has been open since.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Take the thing still carrying that ending and follow it slowly, all the way to where your thinking runs out. Stop there. Do not force a feeling into it.
cells.core:
Something ended here, and you have been treating it as unfinished — the goodbye unsaid, the last call not returned, the thing still half in your hands. Celebration is happening elsewhere, and you are not in it; you are at the doorway of the old room, which closed anyway.

Your own mind can do the rest. Take the thing you keep circling and go all the way into it, deeper than where it usually gets uncomfortable, until it shows you its own edge. You do not have to resolve it. When the pattern stops surprising you, the ending has landed — and the room you are facing can finally be left. Then joy has room again.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is done. You are still at its doorway.
cells.verb: carrying joy that comes alive only when it is shared

cells.tense: You are clearing things for other people and calling it the circumstances of the week.
cells.act: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan
cells.ask: Take the ending you keep tidying around and set your thinking beside your feeling about it, in your own hand, as one plan.
cells.core:
You are clearing something — a room, a schedule, a set of arrangements someone else is standing on — and if asked, you would say it just needed clearing. It did not. You decided it did, and you have been the one doing it, mostly after hours, without the pen.

The joy is being shared out to those nearby except the one keeping the room standing. Put the two sides of what is ending — the thinking and the feeling — on one page together, in your own hand. Not a plan for anyone else. Just your line across it. Once it is there, the ending is yours, and so is whatever gets celebrated after it.
cells.sheetLine: You clear the room and leave your name off it.

attempts.check: The signature says shared joy radiates outward and wants company; the record does not say the person has any community at all, or that any joy is currently being shared, so every cell is written so it stands without either. A reader could say the capacity lives with people and this reading never asks them to find any, which is on purpose, since the medicine's acts are their own and needs no one. The asks survive being wrong about them: each one is a small move with the medicine's own shape, useful whether or not the read lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line claiming what the ending is mourning — so no cell says what was lost, only what is still being carried.
